references.text: The preceding context explaining why a redemption price was necessary—the 273 firstborn Israelites who exceeded the number of Levites had to be redeemed with money.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons according to the Lord's command, completing what was collected in verse 49.
The law concerning the redemption price for the firstborn is repeated, with the same amount of five shekels of silver as mentioned in chapter 3.
The original command to redeem all firstborns, which forms the basis for the redemption system that Moses carries out.
The principle of redemption (pidyon) for Israelites is established, using silver as the payment method to make atonement.
Other provisions regarding redemption money in silver connected to persons dedicated to the Lord.
